summary.text: King of Halicarnassus for whom was built the vast tomb at his city — so notable for its ornament that the Romans call every great tomb a Mausoleum.

story.text: Pausanias, naming the most wonderful graves he knew, singles out the monument at Halicarnassus made for Mausolus, king of the city — of such vast size and ornament that Roman admiration gave his name to every remarkable tomb in their country.
Hyginus counts the monument of King Mausolus among the Seven Wonders of the World — a marble structure eighty feet high and thirteen hundred and forty feet around.
